title: A prospective, randomized comparative study of intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) with proton boost versus standard IMRT in the treatment of head and neck tumors
summary:
Previous studies on various types of cancer have shown that additional radiation with protons—a so-called proton boost—following conventional photon radiation can be at least as effective or even more effective. At the same time, significantly fewer side effects were observed than with standard photon therapy alone.
However, there are currently no meaningful comparative studies for tumors in the head and neck region. Therefore, it is not yet sufficiently clear what specific benefits an additional proton boost actually offers in this area. The aim of the present study is therefore to systematically investigate the safety and efficacy of photon radiation with an additional proton boost compared to standard photon radiation in the treatment of head and neck tumors

interventions.name: Standard IMRT with a total dose of up to 66-70 Gy in 33-35 fractions over seven weeks.
Standard IMRT (50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks) plus pre- or post-boost with protons (up to 16-20 Gy (RBE) in 10 fractions over 2 weeks) to a total dose of up to 66-70 Gy (RBE).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Histologically confirmed head and neck tumor
- Clinical stage I-IVB
- Indication for chemoradiotherapy with a total radiation dose of up to 66–70 Gy (RBE)
- Age ≥ 18 years
- ECOG performance status: 0-2
- Ability to provide informed consent
- Adequate organ function according to laboratory tests
- Willingness to complete quality of life questionnaires and attend regular study visits
- Availability of a written informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
- Malignant neoplasm of the parotid gland (ICD10: C07) or malignant neoplasm of unspecified major salivary glands (ICD10: C08)
- Previous radiation therapy in the head and neck area
- Presence of histologically proven metastatic disease
- Simultaneous participation in another clinical trial that conflicts with this trial
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- unable to give informed consent
